answer: A famous place in my country that I think everyone should see is the National Martyrs' Memorial, which honours those who died in our war of independence in 1971. It is located in Savar, on the outskirts of Dhaka, about an hour's drive from the city centre depending on the traffic. It is a deeply [[poignant]] and symbolic site, and it holds enormous significance for the nation. The memorial itself is architecturally striking, with seven triangular structures of different heights rising towards the sky, and I have read that they represent the key stages of our struggle for independence. It is famous not only for its design but also because every year, on Independence Day and Victory Day, huge crowds come to lay wreaths there, led by the country's leaders. I first visited it on a school trip and went again a few years ago with my younger sister. Visiting it is a genuinely moving experience, as it [[commemorates]] such an important chapter of our history. What makes it so meaningful is that it represents the sacrifice and courage of ordinary people, farmers, students and workers alike. I think it is important for younger generations to visit and understand their [[heritage]]. The surrounding grounds are peaceful and beautifully maintained, with a lake and mass graves nearby, which adds to the [[solemn]] atmosphere. Honestly, I would recommend it to any visitor, ideally early in the morning, because it offers real insight into what shaped our country. It is a place that inspires both reflection and a quiet sense of [[patriotism]].

followUps.q: Do schools in Bangladesh take students there?
followUps.answer: Yes, many schools organise trips there, especially around Victory Day and Independence Day. I think it is a valuable experience, because it helps young people connect emotionally with the history they read about.

followUps.q: Are there other monuments like this in your country?
followUps.answer: Yes, the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka commemorates the Language Movement of 1952. On the twenty-first of February, huge numbers of people walk there barefoot at dawn to lay flowers.
